Settings.AllowMovableGameWindowsTooltip: Hold Ctrl and drag to move windows like your inventory, bank or shop, plus the target frame, party frames and quest tracker. Your layout is saved. Turning this off puts everything back in its default place.
Settings.AutoCloseWindowsTooltip: Opening the Spells, Quests, Party, Friends or Guild window closes your other open windows, so only one is on screen at a time.
Settings.AutoSoftRetargetOnSelfCastTooltip: Using a helpful spell that targets one player (like a heal) while an enemy is selected casts it on you instead, and the enemy stays selected. You can also hold the Soft-Retarget key (Left Alt by default) to do this for one cast. Greyed out if the server has this feature turned off.
Settings.AutoToggleChatLogTooltip: The chat log opens when you start typing and hides again when you finish, keeping your screen clear.
Settings.AutoLootTooltip: Your character walks to loot from your own kills (up to 6 tiles away) and picks it up for you. It won't touch items that belong to anyone else. When your bags are full, only coins are picked up.
Settings.ShareQuestProgressWithPartyTooltip: While you're in a party, your quest progress updates are posted in party chat so your group can see how you're doing.
Settings.AutoTurnToTargetTooltip: When you stand still with a target selected, your character turns to face it after half a second. Greyed out if the server has this feature turned off.
Settings.EnableLightingTooltip: Shows lighting such as night-time darkness, torches, spell glows and the light around your character. Turning it off can help on slower computers. Click Apply to use it.
Settings.EnableScrollingWorldZoom: Enable scrolling to change World Scale in game
Settings.EnableScrollingWorldZoomTooltip: Admin only: use the mouse wheel over the game world to zoom in and out.
Settings.ExtraActionBarTooltip: Adds a second row of 10 action slots (slots 11-20) above your main action bar.
Settings.FpsTooltip: Limits how many frames per second the game draws. V-Sync matches your monitor to prevent screen tearing, lower limits use less power, and No Limit draws as fast as your computer can. Click Apply to use it.
Settings.FullscreenTooltip: Plays the game fullscreen instead of in a window. You can also press Alt+Enter at any time. Click Apply to use it.
Settings.ResolutionTooltip: The size of the game window in pixels. Click Apply to use it.
Settings.ShowChatBubblesTooltip: Shows what nearby players say in local chat as a speech bubble above their heads.
Settings.ShowDamageNumbersTooltip: Shows floating text above characters: damage and healing numbers, Miss, Dodge, Block and Critical, level ups and loot you pick up. Turn this off to hide all of it.
Settings.ShowExperienceAsPercentageTooltip: Shows your experience as a percentage (like 54%) instead of points (like 12,345 / 45,000).
Settings.ShowFPSCounterTooltip: Shows how many frames per second the game is drawing, in the top-right corner.
Settings.ShowFriendOverheadHpBarTooltip: Shows health bars above players on your friends list, even if player HP bars are turned off.
Settings.ShowFriendOverheadInformationTooltip: Shows names above players on your friends list, even if player names are turned off.
Settings.ShowGuildOverheadHpBarTooltip: Shows health bars above members of your guild, even if player HP bars are turned off.
Settings.ShowGuildOverheadInformationTooltip: Shows names above members of your guild, even if player names are turned off.
Settings.ShowHealthAsPercentageTooltip: Shows health as a percentage (like 75%) instead of points (like 450 / 600) on your bars and on target frames.
Settings.ShowManaAsPercentageTooltip: Shows mana or rage as a percentage instead of points, on your bars and on target frames.
Settings.ShowVitalNumbersTooltip: Shows your exact health, mana/rage and experience as numbers on the bars above your action bar. Your action bar sits a little higher so the numbers fit.
Settings.ShowMyOverheadInformationTooltip: Shows your own health and mana/rage bars above your character's head.
Settings.ShowMyOverheadNameTooltip: Shows your own name and guild above your character. Off by default.
Settings.ShowNpcOverheadHpBarTooltip: Shows health bars above all monsters and NPCs. When off, a bar still appears once one is hurt or when you hover over it.
Settings.ShowNpcOverheadInformationTooltip: Shows names above monsters and NPCs. A name always appears when you hover over one.
Settings.ShowPartyOverheadHpBarTooltip: Shows health bars above your party members, even if player HP bars are turned off.
Settings.ShowPartyOverheadInformationTooltip: Shows names above your party members, even if player names are turned off.
Settings.ShowPingCounterTooltip: Shows your connection delay to the server (ping, in milliseconds) in the top-right corner. Lower is better.
Settings.ShowPlayerOverheadHpBarTooltip: Shows health bars above all other players. A bar always appears when you hover over someone.
Settings.ShowPlayerOverheadInformationTooltip: Shows the names of all other players above their heads. A name always appears when you hover over someone.
Settings.StickyTargetTooltip: When on, right-clicking to stop moving or attacking keeps your current target selected; press Esc to clear it. When off, right-clicking also clears your target.
Settings.Title: Settings
Settings.TypewriterTextTooltip: NPC and event dialogue appears word by word, as if it's being typed. Turn this off to show the whole text at once.
Settings.VolumeSoundEffectsTooltip: Volume of sound effects like combat, spells and interface clicks.
Settings.WorldScaleTooltip: Admin only: how zoomed in the game world is. Higher values make everything bigger on screen.
Settings.VolumeWeatherSoundsTooltip: Volume of rain, wind, thunder and other ambient sounds around you.
Settings.PlayerFeedbackEffectsTooltip: The screen edges glow red when your health drops below about 40% (stronger the lower it gets), and the screen flashes briefly when you take damage. Click Apply to use it.
Settings.WorldDepthEnhancementTooltip: Adds soft shadows where walls, objects and characters meet the ground, so the world looks less flat. Maps with their own depth shading are not affected. Click Apply to use it.
Settings.AdminDefaultZoomTooltip: Admin only: the zoom level non-admin characters start at when they log in on this computer.

Tips.ExperienceBody:
Earn XP:
Defeat enemies, complete quests, use XP-granting items, and finish scripted events. Gear with an XP bonus increases the XP you receive.

Level up:
Fill your XP bar to level up. Extra XP carries over, and a large reward can grant several levels at once. Death does not currently remove XP.

Party XP:
Alive party members on the same map and within 40 tiles of the player who lands the kill can share its XP. The XP pool grows with each nearby member before it is divided.

Level differences:
Members close to the killer's level receive the largest share. The farther your level is from the killer's, the smaller your share; a gap of 11 or more gives no XP.
Tips.GroupingBody:
Invite friends:
Right-click a character or chat name and choose Invite to Party. They must accept. A party can hold up to 5 players.

Stay together:
Stay alive and within 40 tiles on the same map to share kill XP. For kill quests, stay within 12 tiles of the defeated enemy on the same map instance and have the matching quest active.

Loot rules:
The leader chooses the rule from the party menu. Shared (default) lets eligible party members claim drops during the ownership timer. Leader Only reserves drops for the leader. Round Robin assigns drops in turn. Free For All makes drops public immediately. Items are not auto-split.

Currency and personal loot:
Currency is shared with the party during the ownership timer, no matter which item rule is selected. Some enemies create separate personal rolls for contributors; a party member who did not contribute may not receive one. Restricted drops become public when the timer ends.
Tips.SkillTreeBody:
Earn skill points:
Start with 1 skill point and gain 1 when you level up. Some quests can award extra points. Skill points are used to rank up passive skills.

Active skills:
Learned abilities appear in the Skills tab. Use them there or drag them to your hotbar for quick access.

Passive ranks:
The Passives tab shows your class's passive tree. Click a node to preview its next rank; the tooltip shows the bonus, rank, and cost.

Unlock and confirm:
A rank may require a level, skill points, or another passive rank. Hover a locked node to see why. Click Confirm to commit your pending choices; leaving the tab clears unconfirmed choices.

Build your way:
Points are limited, so choose bonuses that match your class and play style. Passive effects apply after the upgrade is confirmed.
Tips.RestedBody:
What it does:
Rested XP doubles the XP you earn from defeating enemies while it lasts. Your XP bar turns purple when you have some — hover over it to see the amount. The bonus is spent automatically as you fight.

Earning it:
You build rested XP slowly whenever you are logged out. Logging out inside a rest zone — towns and inns, shown by the moon over your portrait — builds it much faster, and standing in one while playing counts too.

Campfires:
Standing by a lit campfire between 8 PM and 6 AM game time builds rested XP quickly — a nice boost for a night around the fire. It stops at dawn, gives nothing extra while you are logged out, and can only fill a small part of your pool — less for high-level characters.

The limits:
Rest zones can store up to a level and a half of bonus XP. Campfires top off a much smaller amount, so use them for a quick boost between hunts rather than a replacement for a real rest.
Tips.LootingBody:
Pick up items:
Click an item on the ground and your character walks to it and picks it up. You can also press Space to grab the first item at your feet.

Your kill, your loot:
Enemies you defeat stamp their drops with your name. Only you - or your party, while the chosen loot rule allows - can claim them until the ownership timer ends.

Auto-loot:
In Settings > Game > Interface/Gameplay, turn on Auto-loot nearby items. After each kill your character walks to your drops and gathers them one at a time. It only collects loot from your own kills - items other players drop nearby are never touched - pauses the moment you steer elsewhere, and skips anything your bag cannot hold (coins still reach your purse).

Coins:
Copper, silver, and gold go straight into your purse and never fill a bag slot. In a party, coin drops are shared with nearby members automatically.
Tips.CharacterBody:
Opening it:
Press C or use the Character button on the bottom menu to open your character sheet.

What you see:
Your name, level, and class sit at the top. The paper doll shows your equipped gear; hover a slot for an item's stats, and drag or right-click to equip, swap, or unequip. Some gear demands a level, class, or weapon mastery.

The numbers:
The Stats block lists your five core stats - Attack, Ability Power, Defense, Magic Resist, and Agility - totaled from class growth, gear, passives, and buffs.

Details:
The Details panel tracks everything else: your resource (mana or rage), health and mana regen, lifesteal and manasteal, attack speed, cooldown and cast-time reduction, accuracy and evasion ratings, dodge, critical strike, threat, shield block, luck, tenacity, and bonus experience.
Tips.StatsBody:
Attack:
Raises the physical damage of your weapon swings and physical skills.

Ability Power:
Raises spell damage and healing, and shortens cast times - every 20 points cuts casting time by about 1%, up to 30% from this stat alone.

Defense:
Reduces the physical damage you take. Around 100 Defense you take roughly half damage; every point still helps, but each one adds a little less than the last.

Magic Resist:
The same kind of protection, but against spell damage instead of physical hits.

Agility:
Your combat finesse. It feeds Accuracy Rating (your swings land more often) and Evasion Rating (enemy swings miss you more), and keeps your attack animation quick. It does not change your movement speed - only special buffs or rare gear can do that.
Tips.WeaponSkillsBody:
How they work:
Each weapon family trains its own skill - one-handed swords, two-handed swords, one-handed axes, two-handed axes, daggers, staves, bows, and unarmed. You level a skill by fighting with a weapon of that family equipped.

Skill-ups:
Every swing can raise that weapon's skill by 1 - quick at low skill, slower as you near the cap. A separate Defense skill trains instead when physical hits land on you.

The cap:
Skill is capped at 5 times your character level - 250 at level 50. Item bonuses granting +skill push past the cap.

Why it matters:
When you swing, your weapon skill is weighed against the target's defense skill. High skill lands cleaner hits; a brand-new weapon type starts at 1, so expect misses until you train it. Watch for 'Your skill increases' messages in chat, and track your progress on the character window's Weapon Skills tab.
Tips.Title: Tips and Help
Tips.DeathBody:
When you die:
Your body stays where you fell. Release Spirit (or wait out the timer) to rise as a ghost at the map's respawn point - you drift a bit faster but cannot fight, cast, or interact.

Find your body:
Press M for the world map - a skull marks your corpse. The same skull rides the minimap's edge, pointing the way back.

Return to Body:
Stand beside your corpse and choose Return to Body - you revive there with half health and mana, free of any penalty.

Ask Death - at a price:
Death waits near respawn points and revives you instantly where you stand, but you suffer Resurrection Sickness: all stats -50% for 5 minutes (level 10+). A friend with a revive spell can also raise you at your body. Death never takes XP or items.
